articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “I wanted to see what I could do to help her realize her potential”: How Naomi Osaka opened doors for a 9-year-old tennis player from Cameroon
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka has inspired countless young tennis players through her career, but one of her most personal philanthropic efforts began with a 9-year-old.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has inspired countless young tennis players through her career, but one of her most personal philanthropic efforts began with a 9-year-old girl from Cameroon. Uma had watched Osaka play and dreamed of developing her own tennis career. When Osaka heard her story, she wanted to give her an opportunity that could help turn that dream into something real.Through Play Academy with Naomi Osaka, Uma received an individual scholarship to train at the Mouratoglou Tennis Academy in Nice, France. The opportunity gave her access to professional coaching, advanced facilities and other young talents. It also helped her develop habits away from the court, including discipline, focus and following a schedule.How Naomi Osaka learned about Uma’s tennis dream?Play Academy with Naomi Osaka launched in 2020 to create more opportunities for girls through sport. The initiative works with sport-based organisations through grants and training while promoting positive experiences and gender-inclusive coaching.By 2023, Play Academy had expanded to Haiti and Los Angeles and had supported more than 10 grassroots programmes. Uma's scholarship was different because it was the initiative's first individual scholarship of its kind.The young tennis player was from Cameroon and had found inspiration in Osaka's career. Even from thousands of miles away, watching the Osaka play had encouraged Uma to pursue tennis herself.Osaka understood how important those opportunities could be for a young girl. “I know how impactful playing sport at an early age can be, especially for girls who don’t have equal opportunities as boys,” Osaka said.She pointed to several reasons girls can miss out on sport, including a lack of access, safe playing environments and financial limitations.Hearing Uma's story had a particular effect on Osaka because the young girl had been inspired by her despite living so far away.“I felt so humbled and moved when I heard Uma’s story and how watching me play inspired her, even all the way in Cameroon,” Osaka said.That was when Osaka decided to see how she could help Uma move forward.“So I wanted to see what I could do to help her realize her potential,” she said.The scholarship gave Uma the chance to train at the Mouratoglou Tennis Academy in Nice. Instead of only watching the player who inspired her, she could now develop her own game in a professional training environment.For Osaka, the goal was not to guarantee Uma a future in professional tennis. It was to give her access to an opportunity she might otherwise not have had. How Naomi Osaka gave the young tennis player a chance to grow?The Mouratoglou Tennis Academy offered Uma professional coaching and state-of-the-art facilities. She also trained around other junior players and gained experience in an environment built around developing young talent.Her coach, Dario Gioffre, quickly noticed that Uma had unusual ability for her age.“My first impression with Uma was ‘This is unreal.’ You don’t see a 9-year-old hitting that well and being so athletic on the court,” Gioffre said.Her ability surprised him, but he also understood the responsibility that came with coaching such a young player.“I was shocked, in a very positive way, and at the same time I felt a sense of immediate responsibility to work with such potential,” he said.Gioffre did not only focus on Uma's tennis ability. He also noticed her personality and willingness to learn. “The two qualities that come to mind when I think about Uma is happiness,” he said.He described her as someone who was always smiling and also highlighted her curiosity.“She always has questions and is eager to learn,” Gioffre added.The experience helped Uma improve her tennis, but the changes did not stop at her forehand.Uma later thanked Osaka for making the opportunity possible and explained what she had gained from her time at the academy.“I want to say thank you, Naomi Osaka, for making this experience possible at the Mouratoglou Tennis Academy,” Uma said.She said her forehand had improved significantly after one year of training. But she also spoke about lessons that could help her outside tennis.“I have learned a lot of discipline like following a schedule and sticking to it,” Uma said.She also learned how to stay focused when she felt afraid on the tennis court. Those lessons gave the scholarship a purpose beyond improving one young player's technique. Uma was learning how to handle the routine and pressure that come with being an athlete.Naomi Osaka also wanted that development to happen away from the court.“The Mouratoglou Tennis Academy has a wonderful reputation of working with various talents and helping them develop on and off the court,” Osaka said.She added that she was pleased the academy agreed to work with Play Academy to support Uma. The scholarship therefore gave Uma more than better facilities. She had professional guidance, a structured training environment and the chance to learn alongside other young players. How did Uma's scholarship reflect Naomi Osaka’s bigger mission?Uma's story represented exactly the type of opportunity Naomi Osaka wanted Play Academy to create.The initiative was built around helping girls access sport and giving them positive experiences with coaches trained in gender inclusivity. Its work expanded across Japan, Haiti and Los Angeles, but the individual scholarship for Uma showed what that mission could look like when focused on one young athlete.Osaka knew that becoming a successful athlete requires more than talent. Young players need access to coaching, facilities and safe environments where they can develop.Uma had already found motivation by watching Osaka play. The scholarship helped turn that inspiration into an experience of her own.Naomi Osaka was clear about why she wanted to support her. “I wanted to see what I could do to help her realize her potential,” she said.The opportunity also gave Uma a chance to understand what professional training demands. Her comments about following a schedule and staying focused showed that the experience was changing how she approached tennis.Her coach also believed the sport could offer much more to young people than competition.“There’s a whole continent to explore. There’s a whole continent to develop,” Gioffre said.He believes tennis can help children and communities while giving young athletes opportunities to grow.“I strongly believe tennis is a sport for everyone and for life,” Gioffre added.In Osaka’s case, Uma's story was also connected to a larger problem. Girls can lose access to sport because of money, facilities, safety or simply not knowing what opportunities are available to them.Uma had already shown that she wanted to learn. Osaka's scholarship helped give her the environment to do it.For Naomi Osaka, the story began with something simple: a young girl in Cameroon watching her play and finding inspiration in what she saw.And for a 9-year-old who dreamed of becoming better at the sport she loved, that chance was already a significant beginning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paula Badosa gana a Mikulskyte en el SP Open y enamora a Brasil con la camiseta de la 'canarinha'
articles.standfirst: "Me encanta Brasil. Debo decir que en los otros torneos voy con España, pero mi segundo país siempre es Brasil. Tengo una conexión especial, tengo muchos amigos"
articles.summary: "Me encanta Brasil. Debo decir que en los otros torneos voy con España, pero mi segundo país siempre es Brasil. Tengo una conexión especial, tengo muchos amigos"
articles.body: Paula Badosa ganó a la lituana Justina Mikulskyte (número 237 del ranking WTA) para certificar su pase a los octavos de final del SP Open que se disputa en Sao Paulo. "No es fácil, porque no pude entrenar mucho en estas condiciones. Sabía que era un partido difícil. Ella tiene un buen nivel, pero creo que jugué bien; obviamente todavía me estoy adaptando a la altitud. La verdad es que me sentí muy cómoda y estoy feliz con la victoria", explicó Badosa. La tenista española necesitó 1 hora y 15 minutos para imponerse a Mikulskyte por 6-3 y 6-2. Paula Badosa, la actual número 70 del mundo, se enfrentará en siguiente rodan a la argentina Jazmin Ortenzi, situada en el puesto 160 del ranking de la WTA. Paula Badosa se puso la camiseta de Brasil y confesó que se siente como en casa jugando en Sao Paulo. "Me encanta Brasil. Debo decir que en los otros torneos voy con España, pero mi segundo país siempre es Brasil. Tengo una conexión especial, tengo muchos amigos. He venido muchas veces aquí; me siento como en casa. Estoy jugando mi primer WTA aquí en Sao Paulo. Estoy muy feliz", compartió la española.

articles.title: Taylor Townsend undergoes emergency surgery days after completing the career Grand Slam at the US Open
articles.summary: Taylor Townsend has been forced out of the Guadalajara Open after undergoing emergency surgery. Straight from completing the career Grand Slam in doubles at...
articles.body:
Taylor Townsend has been forced out of the Guadalajara Open after undergoing emergency surgery.

Straight from completing the career Grand Slam in doubles at the US Open , she won her opening match against Tatjana Maria.

But Townsend was then forced to withdraw from her match against top seed Marta Kostyuk at the WTA 500 tournament in Mexico.

It has now emerged why, with the American ace sharing a double update on social media after her Guadalajara Open withdrawal.

Taylor Townsend withdraws from Guadalajara after emergency surgery

Posting a message on her Instagram story , she wrote: "Welp… this s— definitely wasn't on my bingo card. Through trials and tribulations… still I rise. I'll update y'all soon."

Townsend then shared a post from the tournament shortly after, which involved a statement that read: "Hi everybody, on the heels of achieving my first career Grand Slam at the US Open, I was so excited to play in front of you all at Guadalajara.

"Because of emergency surgery I am forced to withdraw from the GDL Open, and it breaks my heart. But I'm looking forward to coming back next year to see all of you, the greatest tennis fans. Viva Mexico!"

It's a real shame for Townsend, who is clearly enjoying her time on the court right now, both in doubles and singles.

Taylor Townsend helps Katerina Siniakova claim second career Grand Slam

While Townsend is a very competent singles player, she has just joined the history books thanks to her doubles efforts.

Playing alongside Katerina Siniakova at the US Open, the pair went all the way in New York, defeating American pair Robin Montgomery and Ashlyn Krueger in the final.

Taylor Townsend's Grand Slam doubles finals

The victory helped the duo complete the career Grand Slam, following their titles at Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025, and the French Open earlier this year.

It also meant Siniakova has now claimed her second career Grand Slam, having also achieved the feat playing alongside fellow Czech star Barbora Krejcikova.

images.caption: Taylor Townsend undergoes emergency surgery days after completing the career Grand Slam at the US Open (Photo by Silvia Lore/Getty Images)

articles.title: Ignacio Buse reabre la guerra de sexos del tenis: "El Top 200 ganaría a Rybakina, la número 1"
articles.standfirst: "El tenis de mujeres no se puede comparar, es un deporte distinto, es como el fútbol"
articles.summary: "El tenis de mujeres no se puede comparar, es un deporte distinto, es como el fútbol"
articles.body: El tenista peruano Ignacio Buse, que suma dos títulos en el circuito ATP y que actualmente ocupa el puesto 35 del ranking, ha reabierto la 'guerra de los sexos' en el tenis afirmando en un streaming ante Cristorata que cualquier jugador masculino del top 100 ganaría a Elena Rybakina , la nueva número uno del mundo. Buse, que lidera al equipo de Perú en la Copa Davis ante Paraguay, contestó "hay que respetar, obvio" cuando fue preguntado sobre el resultado de un hipotético partido entre él y Rybakina "Tú, ahora siendo Top 30, ¿le ganarías a la tenista femenina que está en el Top 1?", le preguntaron. "Sí", contestó con seguridad. "Tú, siendo Top 100 o Top 200, ¿le ganarías a la Top 1 del tenis?", le insistieron. "Sí", insistió Buse. Ignacio Buse no se mostró tan seguro de que un Top 1.000 pudiese ganar a la número 1 del Rángking WTA, y matizó que "ahí, cuidado ya. El tenis de mujeres no se puede comparar, es un deporte distinto, es como el fútbol". Elena Rybakina viene de ganar a Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff y Aryna Sabalenka en el último US Open.

images.caption: Ignacio Buse tras ganar el título de Wiston-Salem. ATP Tour

articles.title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Joe Salisbury retires
articles.summary: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
articles.body:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis.

Londoner Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles.

Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

The 34-year-old says he has been thinking about his future for a while, and is now "very happy with the decision".

"Tennis has been my life for as long as I can remember and I have been incredibly fortunate to have had all the opportunities, experiences and success that I have," he posted on Instagram.

"To be able to travel the world and call playing tennis my job has been a dream come true and I never believed I could have lived the life and had the career that I have.

"I gave it my all and know I can be proud and look back with no regrets."

Salisbury took a three-month break at the start of this year, having told BBC Sport about the anxiety which had been affecting him on tour.

While he did not think it affected his tennis very much, he said it left him with a "feeling of dread" which made life on the road far less enjoyable.

Salisbury finishes his career with 17 tour level titles, including the season-ending ATP Finals of 2022 and 2023.

articles.title: Tennis great Patrick McEnroe urges Congress to cap foreign recruits, protect American student-athletes
articles.summary: Patrick McEnroe told Congress that nearly 70% of Division I tennis roster spots now go to international recruits, crowding out American kids.
articles.body: Tennis legend Patrick McEnroe took his fight directly to Capitol Hill this week, urging Congress to cap international athletes on college rosters at 20%. Speaking with OutKick following his testimony before the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, the former Davis Cup captain made his mission clear: stop taxpayer-funded universities from shutting out American kids and restore their focus on developing young domestic talent. "Football and basketball are essentially professional now, and universities are under increasing pressure to fund them," McEnroe told OutKick. "The sports being squeezed are tennis, wrestling and swimming, the Olympic sports that don’t generate revenue." A reality check for college sports The turning point came when McEnroe turned on the SEC Network to watch a college tennis championship and noticed that only two of the 12 players on the court were American. An ACC championship match revealed an even worse ratio, with just one American out of 12. In Division I tennis, international recruits now occupy nearly 70% of roster spots. "This is collegiate tennis, and we’re losing a pathway of dreams and opportunities for American kids," McEnroe said. "I think of it as the rungs on a ladder. If you keep taking away the rungs, the kids will eventually give up." At his academy in New York, McEnroe sees young American athletes grinding every weekend, only to watch collegiate opportunities evaporate as coaches favor older international recruits with professional experience. "Many of those kids dream of playing professionally, but by 14 or 15, they realize that probably won’t happen," McEnroe explained. "What they want is the opportunity to play college tennis, and they’re starting to see that dream disappear. I don’t think that’s right." "That’s why I say I’m not worried about the players who are going to make it," he added. "They represent roughly 1 percent of the people who play college tennis or other college sports and eventually become professionals. This is about the masses." CRUZ AND CANTWELL REFUSE TO BEND TO SEC AND BIG TEN CONCERNS IN REVISED COLLEGE ATHLETICS LEGISLATION Capping international recruits to protect American talent To fix the system, McEnroe is backing a legislative proposal introduced by Rep. Tim Walberg, R-Mich., that would cap international roster spots at 20%. McEnroe believes a firm limit is necessary to give American student-athletes a fairer opportunity. "I don’t believe the purpose of that funding is to give every roster spot to international athletes," McEnroe emphasized. "I’m completely in favor of international athletes participating, but there needs to be a reasonable limit." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He noted that college coaches, trapped in a 'win-now' mentality, are often forced into the recruiting arms race, even if many privately support reform. "I don’t blame the colleges or coaches," McEnroe said. "The system needs guardrails so American kids have an opportunity to play. If the percentage is limited, everyone is on a level playing field." "Many coaches I know won’t publicly support this because they’re afraid of losing their jobs," he added. "That’s why I’m doing it for them. I believe most coaches want a level playing field." For McEnroe, tennis is just the tip of the iceberg in a much broader battle across college sports. "This is a message we should send to young athletes and families in every sport, including soccer and lacrosse," McEnroe added. "In non-revenue Olympic sports, we need to restore some balance to collegiate athletics." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Stop subsidizing overseas competitors The disparity is especially striking when viewed through the lens of the global stage. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, 1,200 NCAA athletes competed, but only 386 were American. More than 800 international athletes trained in U.S. collegiate programs before competing against American athletes at the Olympics. "We have the best training, coaches, facilities and competition in collegiate sports, and we provide all of that to international athletes so they can return home and compete against us in the Olympics," McEnroe argued. "I don’t think that’s what we want taxpayer money supporting." TRUMP URGES CONGRESS TO PASS PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE RECESS: 'WE HAVE TO GET THAT DONE' Capping foreign spots is not an attack on international players. It is a necessary fix to ensure American universities return to their core mission of developing home-grown talent. "I’m an international person," McEnroe concluded. "I’ve been fortunate to travel the world through tennis and make friends everywhere. I love that part of tennis and many other sports. But that doesn’t mean international athletes should completely take over an American collegiate athletic system." articles.title: Este es el orden de juego de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis entre España y Chile: Jódar y Mérida, los individuales
articles.standfirst: La responsabilidad del dobles recae en Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez
articles.summary: Los partidos se disputarán el 19 y 20 de septiembre en el Court Central Anita Lizana de Chile
articles.body: España se juega la clasificación a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24-29 de noviembre) en tierras chilenas. Este jueves se ha hecho efectivo el sorteo del orden de juego para enfrentarse a los de Nicolás Massú en el Court Central Anita Lizana de Chile. Los locales llevan 15 años sin conocer la derrota en su casa. El sábado 19, primer día de la eliminatoria, tendrán lugar dos partidos de individuales. Se enfrentarán el número 2 español, Dani Mérida (41 del mundo), ante el primer espada chileno, Alejandro Tabilo (28). El segundo partido hará que se vean las caras por primera vez sobre la pista el número 1 español, Rafa Jódar (14) y Cristian Garín (133). El domingo 20, segundo y último día de competición, comenzará con el dobles entre Pedro Martínez/Jaume Munar y Tomás Barrios Vera/Alejandro Tabilo. En los individuales, volverán a enfrentarse por tercera vez en la temporada los números 1 de cada país, Rafa Jódar ante Alejandro Tabilo, y los segundos clasificados, Dani Mérida ante Cristian Garín.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner reportedly closing in on deal to hire Juan Carlos Ferrero for 2027 season
articles.summary: Juan Carlos Ferrero is one of the most successful coaches in the modern era. He guided Carlos Alcaraz to six Grand Slam titles and the...
articles.body:
Juan Carlos Ferrero is one of the most successful coaches in the modern era.

He guided Carlos Alcaraz to six Grand Slam titles and the world number-one ranking before departing his team at the end of the 2025 season.

The Spaniard hasn't coached on the ATP Tour since, but Ferrero recently confirmed his plans to return .

And if reports are to be believed, Ferrero could be working alongside his former student's biggest rival next year…

Multiple sources claim Juan Carlos Ferrero will coach Jannik Sinner in 2027

Argentinian journalist Gonzalo Ferreyra shared the following message on X .

"During Cincinnati, Jose Luis Clerc [AKA Batata] hinted that Juan Carlos Ferrero will be Jannik Sinner's coach in the 2027 season. A few hours ago, another source confirmed Batata's information to me," he said.

Jose Luis Clerc was a former Grand Slam semi-finalist. Today he works for ESPN as a commentator and analyst. It's unclear who his sources are, but the tennis world has seemingly caught wind of a potential partnership between Jannik Sinner and Ferrero.

The move would be controversial, to say the least. Sinner and Alcaraz are the two best players in men's tennis and have established a legendary rivalry on tour. If Sinner hires Alcaraz's former coach, who knows how the seven-time Grand Slam champion would take it?

It could be a masterstroke for Sinner. After all, Ferrero knows Alcaraz better than anyone else and has studied the Sinner/Alcaraz matchup for years. Taking everything he learned as Alcaraz's coach to help the Italian, Ferrero could become a major asset to Sinner.

Alcaraz beat Sinner in two Grand Slam finals with Ferrero as his coach, and the world number one will be keen to avoid any more defeats in 2027 and beyond.

Carlos Alcaraz's Grand Slam wins with Juan Carlos Ferrero (6)

Carlos Alcaraz's Grand Slam wins with Juan Carlos Ferrero

Ferrero would likely replace Darren Cahill in Sinner's coaching team. Cahill initially planned to depart at the end of the 2025 season, but was convinced to stay an extra year. If the Aussie leaves this off-season, Ferrero would be a more than adequate replacement.

Working alongside Simone Vagnozzi, Ferrero could help Sinner reassert the dominance he showed earlier this year…

Reviewing Jannik Sinner's 2026 season so far

The world number one failed to win either of the first two tournaments he entered this year, but his winless run didn't last long. Sinner won five consecutive Masters 1000 titles , setting an ATP Tour record before Roland Garros.

Sinner then lost in the second round of the French Open before winning his first Grand Slam of the year at Wimbledon. Suffering a knee injury shortly after, the Italian withdrew from the final major of 2026, the US Open.

Sinner has played exceptionally well this year, but having 'only' won one Grand Slam title, he sits second in the 'Live ATP Race' behind Alexander Zverev. He will need to win big over the coming months to finish 2026 as the world number one.

6 (Wimbledon, Indian Wells, Miami Open, Monte Carlo Masters, Madrid Open, Italian Open)

4 (Canadian Open, Dallas Open, Munich Open, Stuttgart Open)

2 (Dubai Tennis Championships, Brisbane International)

Sinner will return to tennis at the China Open. The Italian is a two-time champion in Beijing and defeated Learner Tien in last year's final.

The 2026 China Open will begin on Monday, September 28.

articles.title: Who are Ben Shelton’s parents? Inside the family background and tennis journey of Bryan and Lisa
articles.summary: International Sports News: Ben Shelton’s rising star in world tennis is rooted in a deep family legacy. His parents, Bryan Shelton and Lisa Witsken Shelton, brought extensive hi.
articles.body: Ben Shelton’s rising star in world tennis is rooted in a deep family legacy. His parents, Bryan Shelton and Lisa Witsken Shelton, brought extensive high-level tennis experience into his life, while his older sister, Emma Shelton, completes a close-knit support system that follows him across the globe. From his father’s transition from tour veteran to full-time coach, to his mother’s standout lineage, family fuels every step of the American’s professional journey.Bryan Shelton: From ATP Veteran to Full-Time CoachBryan Shelton spent nine years on the ATP tour, earning two singles titles and reaching a career-high world ranking of No. 55. His landmark playing moment came at Wimbledon in 1994, where he advanced to the round of 16 as a qualifier. After retiring, Bryan shifted to coaching, winning an NCAA title with the Georgia Tech women’s team before taking over the Florida Gators men’s program. There, he coached Ben to a national team title in 2021 and an individual NCAA singles title in 2022.In June 2023, Bryan stepped down from college coaching to become Ben's full-time traveling coach on the ATP tour. Ben shared a heartfelt tribute on Instagram to celebrate his dad's collegiate career:"My dad retired from collegiate coaching today. Congrats on everything you’ve accomplished in your 24 years out there. This isn’t a career that’s defined by championships and accolades, but by the people impacted and lives changed. You showed up to work every day and gave a perfect effort. You did things with character and humility no matter the situation. You’ve kept your faith wherever your life has taken you, and always put your family first. There isn’t a better role model for young men trying to find their way in life. The Gator Nation may have suffered a blow with this one, but we always bounce back. That being said, the dream team is back together baby Can’t wait to have you out on tour with me, and see what we can accomplish together."Lisa Witsken Shelton and Emma Shelton: The FoundationLisa Shelton was a top junior tennis competitor before pursuing a career in real estate in Gainesville, Florida.Tennis runs deep on her side of the family as well; her late brother, Todd Witsken, was a three-time All-American at USC who achieved world rankings of No. 4 in doubles and No. 43 in singles.Ben's older sister, Emma Shelton, born in March 2001, also competed at the NCAA Division I level, playing for South Carolina and Florida. After graduating in 2023 with a degree in finance, she joined Morgan Stanley as an associate. During Wimbledon, Ben made headlines by asking her employer for extra time off so she could stay and watch his run. Morgan Stanley granted the request, allowing Emma to cheer him on alongside their parents.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Badosa remonta y ya está en cuartos de Sao Paulo
articles.standfirst: La española encajó un primer set que dominaba por 4-1
articles.summary: La española encajó un primer set que dominaba por 4-1
articles.body: Paula Badosa continúa su camino sobre el cemento de Sao Paulo. La española, que esta vez le tocó sufrir, ha tenido que tirar de remontada para eliminar a la argentina Jasmin Ortenzi, número 160 del mundo, por 4-6, 6-2 y 6-2 en su segundo partido en el certamen brasileño. El primer set, que dominaba Paula por 4-1, se lo acabó llevando la joven Ortenzi acumulando cinco juegos seguidos. La gran dinámica de la argentina continuaría con una rotura inicial en la segunda manga, totalmente fuera de los planes de la española. Aunque supo serenarse y respirar en el resto del encuentro. Tan solo cedió un punto con su primer servicio en el tercer set. Se las verá con la americana Mary Stoiana (116) por un puesto en las semifinales. La joven formada en Estados Unidos también sigue su camino en el WTA 250 de Sao Paulo. La abultada victoria ante la local Leme Da Silva, nacida en 2010, por 6-2 y 6-1 la coloca en los cuartos de final. Donde ya la esperaba la serbia Teodora Kostovic, 186 en el ranking.

images.caption: Paula Badosa pega de revés. Sao Paulo Open

articles.title: Carlet acoge el Circuito Juvenil RPT -MARCA by Wilson Sub16 y Sub18
articles.standfirst: Vigésimo novena prueba del circuito de formación más veterano del tenis español
articles.summary: Vigésimo novena prueba del circuito de formación más veterano del tenis español
articles.body: Las magníficas instalaciones del Club de Tenis Carlet ( Valencia), acogerán el “Trofeo Ayuntamiento de Carlet” del 28 de septiembre al 3 de octubre, vigésimo novena prueba del Circuito Juvenil RPT - MARCA by Wilson powered by Ambrosía, con las categorías Cadete - Sub16 y Junior - Sub18, del Circuito Juvenil más longevo del Tenis Español, que este año celebra su trigésimo primer aniversario, organizado por el Registro Profesional de Tenis. Está prueba que por primera vez se celebra en la localidad de Nules, estará dirigida por Jose Luis Sanz, actuando de juez árbitro Oscar García, que coordinarán a los más de 150 participantes que se esperan de toda la geografía española. El torneo cuenta con el apoyo de la Real Federación Española de Tenis, de la Federación de Tenis de la Comunidad Valenciana y el Ayuntamiento de Carlet. Las inscripciones para esta prueba con categorías Sub16 y Sub18 estarán abiertas hasta el lunes 21 de septiembre a las 23 horas, y se pueden realizar única y exclusivamente a través de la nueva web del Circuito: torneos.icisports.org Además, coincidiendo con las rondas finales del torneo, del 2 al 4 de Octubre, se impartirán diferentes cursos de formación y certificación profesional para monitores y entrenadores de tenis, organizados por el Registro Profesional de Tenis, impartidos por Luis Mediero. El Registro Profesional de Tenis - RPT es el más antiguo y mayor promotor del Tenis Juvenil en España, organizando desde 1995 el Circuito Nacional RPT - MARCA by Wilson powered by Ambrosía, que en su 31° edición tendrá 31 semanas de competición con 89 pruebas por toda la geografía española, con el apoyo de la Real Federación Española de Tenis, y la colaboración de Ambrosía, NH hotels, HdI, ICI Sports University y APE deporte. Este año se estima que participen en el Circuito más de 6.000 jugadores. Consulta el calendario 2026 en la nueva web: torneos.icisports.org

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka partners with a controversial brand for multi million dollars days after her 2026 US Open loss
articles.summary: International Sports News: Aryna Sabalenka, the 28 year old Belarusian professional tennis star, might be dealing with her loss in the 2026 US Open after she lost against Elena .
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka, the 28 year old Belarusian professional tennis star, might be dealing with her loss in the 2026 US Open after she lost against Elena Rybakina, in three sets: 6–4, 5–7, 6–2, but she has now signed a new deal which is all set to increase her net worth.Aryna Sabalenka signs an expensive deal with Moroccanoil days after losing in the 2026 US OpenA few days ago, the popular tennis star Aryna Sabalenka signed a multi million deal with the popular haircare brand, Moroccanoil, as she has now become their global brand ambassador.Interestingly, Moroccanoil is also set to sponsor the Miami open which Aryna Sabalenka is now gearing up for.Though it has not been confirmed how much the deal was with the brand, it is reported to be a few multi million dollars.As per reports, the tennis star Aryna Sabalenka earns $23 million from off court deals which has helped in contributing to her massive net worth.A few days ago, in an interview with Cosmopolitan, the Belarusian tennis star opened up about partnering with Moroccanoil as she said, “I’ve used Moroccanoil for years, and when I travel, I see the brand everywhere—from salons to airports,” she says. “I love that the brand is about confidence and feeling your best, because I really connect with that.”She added, “I’m constantly training, competing, sweating, traveling, and then putting it into a tight ponytail, bun, or braid, so I really have to take care of it. I’m not someone who wants to spend hours doing my hair every day, though.”The 28 year old tennis star continued, “I like it to feel healthy, soft, and easy when I’m off the court, which is why I love Moroccanoil. My favorites are products like the Moroccanoil Treatment because they’re so easy to use and you can do a lot with them. I’m always looking for something that makes my routine easier.”Aryna Sabalenka keeps herself out of the spotlight after the 2026 US Open loss as she gears up for the upcoming tournamentsInterestingly, Aryna Sabalenka’s partnership with Moroccanoil has raised some eyebrows as many are concerned about her political affiliations but the tennis star has kept herself away from it.At this point in time, Aryna Sabalenka has remained heartbroken after losing in the 2026 US Open. She has openly expressed her frustration concerning her performance.It seems the 28 year old tennis star is trying to relax for a bit as she has to gear up for the China Open (Beijing) which is all set to begin on September 30 and will end on October 11, 2026.Immediately after that, Aryna Sabalenka’s tour shifts to Wuhan for the final WTA 1000 tournament of the regular season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Naomi Osaka’s tennis outfits mean more than just making a fashion statement
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka has changed more than the pace of a tennis match. In recent years, the four-time Grand Slam champion has made her entrances part of the sp.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has changed more than the pace of a tennis match. In recent years, the four-time Grand Slam champion has made her entrances part of the spectacle, using clothes, accessories and cultural references to reveal a different side of herself. From dramatic couture-inspired outfits to Japanese influences and NBA-inspired streetwear, Osaka has made the court another place to tell her story.Naomi Osaka’s fashion style blends sport, culture and identityOsaka’s approach to fashion became especially visible as she returned to competition after becoming a mother. Her clothing offered her another way to reconnect with her identity, while collaborations with designers and Nike allowed her to bring ideas from outside tennis into the sport.One of the clearest examples came with a gothic-inspired look that Osaka described as almost like stepping into another character.“I feel like we’re all kind of exploring together. It’s not that I have multiple personalities, but every time I wear a different outfit, it’s like a different character, almost like a video game, where you can select different avatars. And for me, it always feels like whatever story we’re telling and whatever outfit I’m wearing, it’s like a different version of myself.”That idea helps explain why her outfits rarely feel random. They often carry a reference, a memory or a piece of her personality.At the Australian Open, Osaka took that approach even further with a look inspired by a jellyfish. Created with London designer Robert Wun and Nike, the ensemble included a flowing veil, a wide-brimmed hat and a sheer parasol. Butterfly details also nodded to a memorable moment from her past when a butterfly landed on her face during a match.Osaka explained why these moments matter to her beyond the clothes themselves.“When I look back at the players who came before me, I think about how those moments—those looks—have become memories that live forever […] So much of the time, other people get to write our stories for us. This felt like a moment where I could write a little bit of my own.”Her Grand Slam wardrobe has continued to shift with the setting. At Indian Wells, she embraced bold animal print. At Roland Garros, she wore a shimmering gold design that drew inspiration from the Eiffel Tower. Wimbledon brought a more traditional white palette, but Osaka still found room for personal meaning through a Japanese-inspired kimono wrap.“I’ve never thought of the colour white as a restriction”, Naomi said at the pre-tournament press conference, “there are so many different patterns and textures that you can use. It doesn’t hinder me.”She also explained the cultural connection behind her Wimbledon outfit.“My Japanese heritage means a lot to me… so I thought it would be cool to come out in a kimono.”Naomi Osaka uses fashion to challenge tennis traditionsOsaka’s fashion choices have not gone unnoticed. Some traditionalists have questioned whether elaborate walk-on outfits belong in tennis, particularly when players are expected to follow long-established dress traditions.After one match, Laura Siegemund criticised the idea, saying, “I come here to play tennis, not to put on a fashion show.”Osaka has made it clear that pleasing everyone is not the purpose of her style.“There’s a demographic that’s been talking about ‘traditional’ tennis outfits… I don’t do this for them though, they will never get it and I don’t want them to. I do this for the people that are like me”, she addressed on social media. “I don’t mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it. This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it’s happening with my clothes. I’m literally Haitian, it’s in my blood to be this way—as long as the people after me have an easier path, it’s worth it.”Her fashion also reflects influences beyond tennis. Osaka has cited NBA icon Allen Iverson as an inspiration, particularly because of the way he helped reshape how basketball players expressed themselves through clothing.At the US Open, Osaka paid tribute to Iverson with a look featuring a grey hoodie, white skirt, armband and headband. She explained his influence simply:“He’s someone that I look up to a lot”, she told reporters at a press conference before the tournament. “He’s kind of done a lot in fashion, whether it’s on purpose or not, but he’s shifted the way that NBA players dress.”For Osaka, fashion has become more than a collection of striking outfits. It gives her control over how she presents herself, connects her sporting career with her heritage and creates memories for fans before a ball is even struck.Her influence now stretches across tennis, fashion and popular culture. Each entrance offers something different, but the message remains consistent: Osaka wants athletes to have room to be themselves, both on the court and beyond it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “They told me I wasn’t fit enough to play, but my body carried me through this.” - How Taylor Townsend overcame body shaming and racial bias to become tennis champion
articles.summary: International Sports News: Taylor Townsend has come a long way from being a 16-year-old tennis star whose body became a subject of debate inside American tennis. In 2012, Townse.
articles.body: Taylor Townsend has come a long way from being a 16-year-old tennis star whose body became a subject of debate inside American tennis. In 2012, Townsend was the No. 1 junior in the world, but the USTA questioned her fitness and stopped its support around the US Open. She paid her own way to New York and still won the junior doubles title. More than a decade later, Townsend became a Wimbledon champion with Kateřina Siniaková in 2024. In 2026, the pair completed their career Grand Slam by winning the US Open, adding another major chapter to Townsend’s story.What happened between Taylor Townsend and the USTA when she was the No. 1 juniorTownsend was only 16 when she reached the top of the junior rankings in 2012. She had already won the Australian Open junior singles and doubles titles and then added the Wimbledon junior doubles title. Her results made her one of the biggest young names in American tennis.Then came the dispute that changed how she saw the sport.The USTA wanted Townsend to spend time working on her fitness rather than playing at the junior US Open. The organisation’s officials said they were concerned about her long-term health and development. Townsend, however, felt that her body had become the main focus despite what she was achieving on court.There was also another part of the story. Townsend was later found to have low iron and anemia, which had affected her energy. She eventually received medical clearance, but by then the issue had already caused serious damage to her relationship with the organisation. Her mother, Sheila, helped her get to New York.Townsend did not simply attend the tournament. She made the most of the chance she had fought to keep. She reached the junior singles quarterfinals and won the doubles title with Gabrielle Andrews.Years later, Townsend described the experience in The Players’ Tribune in very direct terms:“I was fat, and I was Black, so they took away my dream. Or at least they tried.”She also explained how difficult it was to be judged so publicly as a teenager.“Being a teenage girl, having to talk about her body, her weight, like on a worldwide stage. It was always a topic of conversation.”How did Taylor Townsend deal with race, body image and pressure in tennisThe USTA dispute did not disappear once Townsend became a professional. The experience followed her as she tried to build a career in a sport where she often felt different from the image people expected an elite player to have.Townsend grew up on Chicago’s South Side and became a Black girl competing at the highest level of junior tennis. Her style was also different. She liked moving forward, attacking at the net and taking the ball early instead of relying only on long baseline rallies.The pressure around her appearance became difficult to separate from tennis itself. In her own account of those years, Townsend said she felt that she was being pushed to fit a certain image instead of being allowed to develop as the player she was.But she did not leave the sport. She kept building her career and eventually became a regular presence on the WTA Tour.That history also helps explain why her later success meant more than another trophy. Townsend was no longer trying to prove that she could fit someone else’s idea of a tennis player. She was playing on her own terms.How did motherhood change Taylor Townsend’s career after son Adyn was bornTownsend became pregnant in 2020 and gave birth to her son, Adyn Aubrey, in March 2021. She then spent about 18 months away from competitive tennis.That break changed more than her schedule. It changed the way she looked at the sport.In a 2025 interview with Women’s Health, Townsend said becoming a mother helped her step away from the pressure she had carried for years. She said she had spent so much of her life trying to prove herself that she needed the distance to understand what she actually wanted from tennis.“Coming back to tennis after having my son, Adyn, really gave me that freedom to grow into the authentic person I am now.”She also explained that motherhood gave her a different sense of purpose.“As a mom, I have a sense of purpose outside of my sport. I know that winning and losing tennis matches isn’t everything.”That change was visible when she returned. Townsend was still ambitious, but tennis was no longer the only thing defining her.She also became more open about the physical and emotional challenges of returning after childbirth. Instead of hiding the difficult parts, she shared parts of the process publicly. That made her comeback different from the one she might have imagined as a teenager.How did Taylor Townsend become a Grand Slam champion with Kateřina SiniakováTownsend’s first Grand Slam women’s doubles title finally arrived at Wimbledon in July 2024. She teamed up with Czech star Kateřina Siniaková, and the pair beat Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe in the final.It was Townsend’s first Grand Slam title at the professional level after earlier runner-up finishes at the 2022 US Open and 2023 French Open. The victory came three years after Adyn’s birth.After winning, Townsend kept the reaction simple:“This is my first one, my first Grand Slam title. I’ve been close two other times. To get over the finish line the way that we did, I think we played so well.”The Wimbledon trophy was only the beginning of what became a remarkable partnership. Townsend and Siniaková went on to win the Australian Open in 2025, the French Open in 2026 and then the US Open in September 2026.Their US Open victory completed the career Grand Slam as a team. Townsend’s achievement is now much bigger than the Wimbledon breakthrough that first put her name on a major trophy.For a player who once had to pay her own way to a junior tournament after being told she was not ready, the contrast is hard to miss. Townsend did not change her story by becoming someone else. She kept playing, became a mother, returned to the biggest stages and eventually collected every women’s doubles Grand Slam with Siniaková.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: ‘My biggest bet would surely be the doubles’ - Neha Aggarwal Sharma on India’s table tennis medal hopes
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India’s 10-member table tennis contingent is already in Japan, with the Aichi-Nagoya competition for the event beginning on September 20. At the foref.
articles.body: India’s 10-member table tennis contingent is already in Japan, with the Aichi-Nagoya competition for the event beginning on September 20. At the forefront are world No. 3 men’s doubles pair Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah, while India also has experience in Sathiyan Gnanasekaran and Harmeet Desai, and a younger group featuring Sreeja Akula, Yashaswini Ghorpade, Diya Chitale and Syndrela Das.For Neha Aggarwal Sharma, the difference between this Indian team and the one she was part of at the 2014 Asian Games is hard to miss.“I remember when I played at the 2014 Asian Games, we lost in the quarterfinals. We played against China. It was a close match.”“We lost a few others. I mean, we weren't really expected to win medals and it was okay. And now cut to 2026, if you look at, say, my sport, table tennis in particular, we are going in as the world number three in men's doubles,” Sharma told Timesofindia.com in an exclusive interaction facilitated by Sony Sports Network.12 years on, the expectation around Indian table tennis has changed. Sharma sees it not only in the rankings and results, but in how the players approach international competition.“The sort of improvement that India has seen is phenomenal. And I think that mindset shift is what is, to me as an athlete, what we need to see. And we are seeing now for India, Indian sports overall.”For table tennis specifically, however, Sharma is not suggesting the job is done. India has moved up the rankings, won at the WTT Feeder level and started collecting medals at Contenders. However, against China, Japan and Korea, the consistency is still missing.“We are winning, say, at the WTT level, we are winning feeders. We are now winning medals at the Contenders, we have had some good performances at the [WTT] Star Contenders as well. But I think we are not consistently beating China, Japan and Korea.“You would see one-off wins here and there. But for us to really bridge that gap, I think it is going to take another generation to do that,” assessed the 2008 Olympian.Doubles carries the clearest medal opportunityThe strength of this Indian squad is spread across the doubles events, and for Sharma, that is where India can realistically challenge for medals and build towards the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.“Firstly, we have to start building the narrative for mixed doubles and men's and women's doubles. Why? it is at the Olympics now, very simple. And even if you talk from LA perspective, these are the events which are our genuine medal chances.”“So, even, not to put pressure on Manav, Manush, Dia, Yashaswini, but genuinely we have chances,” quipped the former No. 1 ranked Indian paddler.India also has a recent Asian Games reference point in women’s doubles. Sutirtha Mukherjee and Ayhika Mukherjee had won a historic bronze at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.“Last time, if you recall, Suteertha and Ahika had won the bronze in the women's doubles. So that's one clear, clear medal chance,” said Sharma.Men’s team has experience around Manav and ManushThe men’s team combines the current form of Manush and Manav with the experience of Sathiyan and Harmeet. Sathiyan has been a mainstay of Indian table tennis for more than a decade, and Sharma believes his experience can have a role in the team event.“Manush is in fantastic form. Manav has been doing great as well, and it is good to see Sathiyan back. He had a bit of a downfall the last two years, but very, very happy to see [him back] because his experience will count quite a lot from the team's perspective.”India’s women’s team, meanwhile, has a different task. Sharma recalled the previous Games, when India lost to Thailand in the round of 16.“I think this time, if we get past that round of 16, once you're in the quarterfinals, you'll have China, Japan, Korea and I think Hong Kong or Singapore, either of these four countries, depending on the draw. There it's anybody's game, in my opinion, so it is possible.”And she believes the men have the stronger team-event chance.“I do believe the men have a better chance in the team events than the women do.”But when asked where she would put her strongest medal call, Sharma went back to the doubles.“We can surely get medals in the team events as well. But my biggest bet would surely be the mixed doubles and men’s and women’s doubles events.”The Manika Batra gapThere is also a conspicuous absence from India’s women’s team. Manika Batra was left out of the Asian Games squad after not meeting the selection criteria, with her absence from domestic events meaning she did not feature in the TTFI’s national rankings. Batra publicly questioned the consistency and transparency of the selection process and sought a detailed explanation from the federation.It has left India without one of its most experienced women’s players for the Asian Games - and Sharma was careful not to let the selection row overshadow what the team taking the court in Japan can do.“Keeping the controversy aside, see, I think Manika has really asserted her position in world table tennis as somebody who can beat anybody at any time.”“You can see from 2018 onwards, that's when she rose. And till now, you keep seeing these one-off wins. And when we spoke about consistency, right? Like Manika has been able to consistently beat world top 20 players.”For Sharma, Batra’s value also comes from her ability to handle pressure and the way her presence can affect an opponent.“She is one player who performs well under pressure. You need those players in your team. Second, also similar is Sreeja.”But Sharma emphasised that the focus has to be on the players who will be in Japan.“We will miss Manika. But yes, players like her just boost the morale in a different way. Even from the opponent's perspective that, you know, somebody like her is there. But having said that, I just feel that let's not get into all of that.”“Let's focus on who we have. Sreeja is just fresh off of winning the feeder at Puerto Princesa. I think, even somebody like a Syndrela Das, she just plays her heart out.”Divyanshi and Syndrela lead the next generationThere is a wider point to Sharma’s argument about the gap with China, Japan and Korea. India has had players such as Sharath Kamal and Manika Batra who could produce results at the highest level.Now, Sharma is looking at the teenagers coming through behind them - among them Divyanshi Bhowmick and Syndrela, two players she believes have the game and mindset to eventually challenge the best in Asia.Syndrela is already in Japan with the Asian Games squad; Bhowmick figures in Sharma’s assessment of the larger pipeline.“To build a generation of athletes, say, for example, a Divyanshi Bhowmick or a Syndrela Das, right, at respectively 15 and 17 years old, the sort of game that they have and the mindset that they have, they are really the ones who can consistently be there at the level where we can beat our top class of China, Japan, Korea.”Sharma pointed to the number of young Indian players now competing at WTT events.“Because I can already see the next crop coming up. Just the number of players that have increased in terms of participation. I mean, it's fantastic the number of players who are playing at the under-15 and under-17 level at the WTT levels.“They're spending from their own side and going and taking part in tournaments. It's heartening to see that.”And when asked which Indian table tennis players she was most interested in watching at the Games, Sharma returned to Syndrela and the men’s doubles pair.“In table tennis, I am very excited about... One is Syndrela Das. And second is for Manav and Manush to either get us the men's doubles. Or in the men's team, to see those wins.”(Watch Asian Games 2026 live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Felix Auger-Aliassime now confirms what happened to him at the US Open after second-round defeat
articles.summary: Felix Auger-Aliassime lost to Karen Khachanov, 7-6, 3-6, 2-6, 2-6, in the second round of the 2026 US Open. The Canadian reached the US Open...
articles.body:
Felix Auger-Aliassime lost to Karen Khachanov, 7-6, 3-6, 2-6, 2-6, in the second round of the 2026 US Open.

The Canadian reached the US Open semi-finals a year ago, but failed to repeat the feat in 2026. Instead, Khachanov defeated Auger-Aliassime in four sets before reaching the semi-finals himself.

Auger-Aliassime looked off his game at Flushing Meadows, and ahead of this weekend's Davis Cup action, he's confirmed what really happened to him.

Felix Auger-Aliassime thinks he may have been suffering from 'heatstroke' during US Open defeat

During an interview with the Davis Cup media team, Auger-Aliassime said the following about his US Open exit.

"Obviously, after what happened in New York, first you have to digest the loss and the disappointment; then I always try to figure out what happened. In this case, it was not easy to find out what happened. I think it was some sort of heatstroke or something, really out of my control," he said.

"You just have to move on, have to learn how to move on fast, not dwell on it too much, and bounce back. This is now my next event after the US Open, and I'm going to try to play some good tennis!"

Auger-Aliassime finished 2025 in some of the best form of his career, leaving many wondering if he could challenge Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner at this year's Grand Slam tournaments. Unfortunately for the Canadian, he couldn't maintain the level he showed last fall and didn't reach a major semi-final this season.

Felix Auger-Aliassime's 2026 Grand Slam results

Australian Open – First round (Lost to Nuno Borges)

French Open – Quarter-final (Lost to Flavio Cobolli)

Wimbledon – Quarter-final (Lost to Novak Djokovic)

US Open – Second round (Lost to Karen Khachanov)

The good news for Auger-Aliassime is that he is about to begin his favourite stretch of the season. The 26-year-old often excels after the US Open, especially at the indoor hard-court tournaments.

First up is a Davis Cup qualifying tie against the French…

Felix Auger-Aliassime previews Davis Cup qualifier vs France

Auger-Aliassime, Canada's star man, is expected to lead his team to victory over France in Quebec. The world number six is excited to play in front of his home fans again after missing this year's Canadian Open.

"My dad still has an academy here; it's nice to have a chance to see my people, have a chance to come back to the courts I grew up on. And to know that I'm actually going to play here and I'm not just visiting is quite nice," he said.

"So I think we're going to have an amazing atmosphere, an amazing moment, and hopefully some good tennis and the win; that would be great."

Auger-Aliassime missed Canada's 3-2 win over Brazil in February, but kept a close eye on his teammates.

"Coming back to Liam [Draxl] and Gab [Diallo] playing in Brazil earlier this year, I was actually over in Europe, so it was tough to watch live, but I was in touch with Gab, in touch with the rest of the team, wishing them the best, following the scores, seeing a few clips whenever I could," he said.

"The sense of playing for something bigger than yourself is something I take a lot of pride in. On tour, it's more individual, but once in a while, you get a chance to play for something much bigger; I do enjoy that."

Finally, Auger-Aliassime commented on Canada's stunning 2022 Davis Cup triumph, where he clinched the title with a straight-sets win over Alex de Minaur.

"When I look back at 2022, what stays the most is obviously the win, the final moment. These are moments that you cherish forever, we had an amazing campaign, an amazing journey throughout the year. It started out tough, but then we picked it up in September, played some great tennis," he said.

"The team was a little bit different – different players – but everything kind of came together; everything clicked, and we got out of tough situations in certain ties. Once we made it out of that, and we came to the end of the year, it was the quarter-final stage; we needed three ties to win it all, and we felt that this week could be the week where we make history in our country.

"It would be nice to have a chance to feel that again; it could take a bit more time, if we're realistic. What we did was extra special; everything kind of had to click and come together, so it's going to be a lot of adversity going through that again, but I believe in myself, and I believe in the team, that it's something we can do again."

Auger-Aliassime and Team Canada must beat France to advance to this year's Davis Cup Finals in Bologna. Their qualifying tie will take place on Friday, September 18, and Saturday, September 19.

articles.title: Davis Cup 2026: Cameron Norrie out for GB as Arthur Fery leads team against Ecuador
articles.summary: Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.
articles.body:
Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.

British number two Norrie felt pain in his arm during a practice session and will be replaced in Saturday's singles by world number 95 Toby Samuel.

"He wasn't able to accelerate on the ball like he wanted to," Davis Cup captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport.

"It's nothing major, but there's still a lot of tennis to be played this year and with that in mind, we had to make the difficult decision to replace him."

Great Britain have not reached the knockout stage of the competition since 2023, and they will have to do so this time with an inexperienced team.

Jack Draper has ended his difficult season early, while Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley are both unavailable with injury.

It means Samuel will make his Davis Cup debut against Andres Andrade in Saturday's first match, with British number one Arthur Fery following against Alvaro Guillen Meza.

Both of Ecuador's singles players are outside the world's top 200, but Fery's only previous appearance for his country was in Poland last September.

Asked if he was concerned about the lack of experience, Smith said: "I'm not sure it concerns me, but it is obviously a factor.

"Neal [Skupski] is in the team, Cam is staying with the team. I've had 16 years at this so I can hopefully help a little bit.

"But you want them to experience this. You have to start somewhere and I have a lot of confidence in Arthur, Toby and our doubles team.

"If they can put out the level of tennis we've seen over the course of the summer and before that, they'll give themselves a good opportunity."

British number seven Harry Wendelken, who is at a career-high world ranking of 175, was at the Copper Box as a practice partner and has been added to the team in Norrie's absence.

World number one Henry Patten will team up with new US Open champion Neal Skupski for Sunday's doubles, which precedes two reverse singles.

Coverage from 13:00 BST on 19 September and 12:00 BST on 20 September

In July, Fery played on Wimbledon's Centre Court in a men's singles semi-final, but this will be the first time he has played for his country as the British number one.

He lost in the first round of the US Open in August but reached the Winston-Salem final in the build-up to the final Grand Slam of the season.

"I'm aware of the role I have as the number one player and I am representing my country, so there's always a little more responsibility," Fery told BBC Sport.

"But at the same time I've been able to deal with high-pressure situations a lot of times this year and I feel like I've done a great job with them. Tomorrow isn't going to be any different to that.

"I think there's no shying away from it - if I want to do great things in tennis and push on, be top 20 or top 10, I have to take this responsibility on.

"I'm ready to do that and represent my country. It's something new but something that I feel comes with the player I'm becoming."

Great Britain beat Norway 4-0 in the first qualifying round in February and are trying to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 2023.

Ecuador may be the underdogs, but they were in the same role when they beat Australia comprehensively in February.

And they have won, famously, on British soil before. Ecuador beat a British team that contained Tim Henman and Greg Rusedski 3-2 on Wimbledon's Court One in July 2000.

The seven winners of this weekend's qualifying ties will join three-time defending champions Italy in the final eight stage in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

"We've missed not being at that stage and it's up to us now to take that opportunity," Smith added.

"We have a good opportunity. It's never ever straightforward, despite what people might look at in the rankings - just ask Australia what happened in February.

"We're on it, we've got a good team, and we'd be thrilled to get to the finals."

articles.title: Rybakina no jugará la Billie Jean King Cup ante España tras ganar el US Open
articles.standfirst: La kazaja no se recupera del todo de unas molestias del tendón de Aquiles que sufre desde el torneo de Cincinnati
articles.summary: La kazaja no se recupera del tendón de Aquiles y anuncia su baja de la eliminatoria
articles.body: Las finales de la Billie Jean King Cup (22-27 de septiembre) han perdido a su mayor atractivo, Elena Rybakina. La reciente campeona del US Open, derrotando a Aryna Sabalenka en la final, no está recuperada de las molestias en el tendón de Aquiles que la forzaron a retirarse en el Masters 1000 de Cincinnati ante Iga Swiatek. Kazajistán no contará con la reina del circuito femenino de cara a su eliminatoria de cuartos de final ante España el 23 de septiembre en la ciudad china de Shenzhen. La jugadora, que pasará pruebas médicas en Kazajistán, ha hablado en sus redes sociales y desea mucha suerte a sus compañeras de equipo: "Hola a todos. Debo anunciar que no podré participar en la Billie Jean King Cup este año. Me entristece mucho no estar en Shenzhen, una ciudad y un público tan increíbles. El último mes ha sido duro para mi cuerpo y necesitaré recuperarme y estar en mi mejor versión para volver a competir. Les deseo a mis compañeras mucha suerte". Por parte de las kazajas, jugarán: Yulia Putintseva, Sonja Zhiyenbayeva, Zhibek Kulambayeva y Anna Danilina. Cristina Bucsa, Jessica Bouzas, Kaitlina Quevedo, Marina Bassols y Sara Sorribes formarán el equipo español. La Federación de Tenis de Kazajistán emitió un comunicado hablando de la situación de su deportista y el uso de analgésicos para poder competir en el grande neoyorquino: "La lesión en el tendón de Aquiles continuó complicando a Rybakina en el US Open. Sin embargo, a pesar del dolor, Elena se alzó con el título disputando los partidos finales bajo los efectos de analgésicos". En su estancia en Astaná y Almaty, Rybakina impartirá charlas a jóvenes atletas.

articles.title: Shelton juega para Estados Unidos pero pierde ante el checo Lehecka
articles.standfirst: El finalista del US Open quiso representar a su país cinco días después de la final del US Open
articles.summary: El finalista del US Open quiso representar a su país cinco días después de la final del US Open
articles.body: En la eliminatoria más atractiva de los playoff clasificatorios para las Finales de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre), la República Checa y Estados Unidos empatan a uno tras la disputa de la primera jornada de competición. Ben Shelton, número cuatro mundial y flamante finalista del US Open, en la final que cedió el domingo con Alexander Zverev, quiso alinearse con Estados Unidos apenas cinco días después. Se borró, en cambio, de la Laver Cup de Londres que se celebra el próximo fin de semana en la capital británica. El resultado fue derrota en dos sets ante Jiri Lehecka, por un doble 6-4, que iguala la serie en la que Learner Tien había adelantado a los visitantes gracias a su triunfo frente a Jakub Mensik, por 6-2 y 6-4. El tercer punto del dobles, programado para la apertura de la jornada del sábado, se presenta decisivo. Los locales han anunciado un dúo formado por Adam Pavlasek y Patrick Rikl mientras que los americanos apuestan por Christian Harrison y Austin Krajicek. En la serie más descafeinada, Corea del Sur supera con relativa facilidad a la India, por 2-0, con los puntos de Soonwoo Kwon y Hyeon Chung. Austria y Bélgica empatan a uno con los triunfos de Jurij Rodionov y Zizou Bergs.

articles.title: El equipo español de Copa Davis sufre el terremoto en Santiago de Chile
articles.standfirst: El combinado español vivió en primera persona un sismo de magnitud 4,7 en la capital chilena
articles.summary: El combinado español vivió en primera persona un sismo de magnitud 4,7 en la Región Metropolitana.
articles.body: La ciudad de Santiago de Chile ha vivido este viernes un terremoto de magnitud 4.7 en mitad de la sesión de entrenamiento del equipo español de la Copa Davis, según ha podido saber MARCA. Rafa Jódar se estaba ejercitando en ese momento en la pista central con su compañero Jaume Munar. Ellos dos no se han percatado del sismo. Sí se dieron cuenta los responsables de la Federación Internacional de Tenis, que han acudido rápidamente a la cancha principal para informar que se habían movido las paredes.
